steps.text: I'm June, Maya's aunt. Her birthday is this week and I want to give her $300. Should I just send her the cash? She's on SSI, and her family made a Giftwise page for her: maya.

Gift page for Maya (/g/maya). Open needs: Wheelchair repair: $420 still needed, paid to Riverside Mobility Repair; Laptop for college: $649 still needed, paid to Eastgate College Bookstore; Electric bill, this month: $138 still needed, paid to Maya's ABLE account; Therapy co-pay: $90 still needed, paid to Northside Physical Therapy. Any amount can also go to her ABLE account.

Cash counts as income. $300 minus $80 in exclusions leaves $220 counted in November, so their January check would be $774. Giving the item itself keeps $994. Sources: 20 CFR 416.1121: types of unearned income, including gifts; POMS SI 00830.520: Gifts; POMS SI 00810.410: Infrequent or Irregular Income Exclusion; POMS SI 00810.420: $20 General Income Exclusion; POMS SI 02005.001: Retrospective monthly accounting.
$300 for Maya: $300 to Riverside Mobility Repair (Wheelchair repair). Her check stays $994. Given as cash, it would be $774.

June, it's lovely that you're doing this for Maya. I'd hold off on sending cash, though.

If you send $300 in cash, Social Security counts it as income. That would lower her monthly check for January from $994 to $774. She'd lose $220 of her benefits, so the gift would really be worth only $80 to her.

Instead, I suggest sending the $300 straight to Riverside Mobility Repair to pay for part of her wheelchair repair. That's one of the needs on her Giftwise page, and they still need $420. Paying the shop directly doesn't count as income, so her check stays at $994 and all $300 helps her.

Would you like me to set up a PayPal checkout that way? Once you say yes, I'll make it and send you the link. Nothing will be charged until you approve it in PayPal yourself.
That makes sense. Yes, please set up the $300 that way.

PayPal checkout ready for $300 to Maya, paid to 1 recipient. The person giving should open this link and approve in PayPal: [PayPal approval link]. After they approve, the receipt will be at /r/[receipt].

Your $300 checkout is ready, June. PayPal's own record shows one payment of $300.00 for Maya's wheelchair repair, and it's waiting for you to approve it.

If you sent the $300 as cash, her monthly check would drop from $994 to $774. Paying the repair shop directly keeps her check at $994, so all of your gift helps her.

To finish, open this link and approve the payment in PayPal:
[PayPal approval link]

Nothing is charged until you approve it. This is a test version of PayPal, so no real money will move. After you approve, your receipt will be here:
/r/[receipt]

What a thoughtful birthday gift. I hope Maya has a wonderful day.
